ios.desc:
Once gives you one thing per day.

When you open the app, you receive a single thing. Maybe a thought, a word, a sound, a question, or maybe something harder to define. After that, the app locks until the next calendar day.

There is no scrolling, no feeds, no history, and no retries. What you see is what you get. Once.

Once gives you a moment, then gets out of the way. Sometimes calm, sometimes uncomfortable, sometimes thought-provoking. It asks nothing from you except a brief glance.

Open it. Experience it. Come back tomorrow.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Once – An app that only works once per day

quotes.text:
I built an iOS app that intentionally limits usage to once per day.

Open it, get one piece of content (text, sound, color, etc), then it locks until the next calendar day. No feed, no history, no notifications, no data collection.

Built it as a response to infinite scroll fatigue. Not sure if there's a market for anti-engagement apps, but feedback from early users has been positive.

Would love feedback from HN on the concept and execution.
